title: F5: Structured reporting and message ids in Python
description: messageIds becomes a required manifest field (T1) and the behavioural conformance corpus (T12) asserts a messageId plus data payload per finding, so Python must report structurally instead of pre-formatting a sentence at the call site. report() gains a message-id-plus-data form and each rule declares the ids it can emit. Wide but shallow: 20 self.report call sites plus ML400's direct Violation construction, and 17 of 19 rules emit exactly one message. Violation.format's output stays byte-identical - the rendered sentence is still what users see, now produced from the id and the data rather than passed in.
acceptance_criteria: Every rule declares a non-empty messageIds, asserted by a test rather than left to review. Rendered output byte-unchanged for every rule's bad_example, asserted by test. Lands before T3, which serialises the field.

title: F4: Rename Rule.code to Rule.id across the Python package
description:
See docs/typescript-port.md#F4. D1 named the manifest field 'id' (ESLint's word for @ml-lints/ML500 is the rule ID, and 'code' collides with badExample/goodExamples, which hold literal source code). Rather than leave a permanent seam where the manifest says 'id' and Python says 'code', rename the Python side to match.

Scope: RuleCode StrEnum -> RuleId (violation.py); Violation.code -> Violation.id; Rule.code ClassVar (rules/__init__.py:69) and its 19 rule-module assignments; cls.code readers in runner.py:35, cli.py:312-519, rules/__init__.py:91-95; has_noqa's 'code' parameter (noqa.py:12); both rule templates (src/ml_lints/rules/_template.py, tests/rules/_template.py); scripts/generate_rule_docs.py and generate_rules_table.py; tests/. Prose in README.md and CONTRIBUTING_RULES.md (:24 'Rule code ranges', :51, :168-177).

NOT in scope, because these carry the value rather than the field name and renaming them would be a user-visible break: the '# noqa: ML100' suppression syntax, and Violation.format()'s 'path:line:col: ML100 message' output.

Land this BEFORE T3 (mlp-v00.4) so the manifest emitter reads rule.id directly with no mapping line, and so T1's seam paragraph is deleted rather than implemented.

Collision risk: justfile:101's inline 'python3 -c' scaffolding hardcodes the '# -- add new codes above this line --' sentinel in violation.py and prints 'RuleCode.${code}'. It must move in lockstep. A1 (language-aware scaffolding) plans to extract that same one-liner into scripts/scaffold_rule.py — whichever lands second rebases onto the first.

Note: ruff's A003 does not fire on 'id' as a class attribute under this project's select=["ALL"] config — verified empirically, so the rename is not blocked by linting.
acceptance_criteria: No 'code' identifier remains as a rule-identifier field name in src/, scripts/ or tests/ (grep-verified); RuleCode is RuleId. 'just new-rule ML999' still scaffolds a working rule and injects the enum member. 'just precommit' green. The suppression syntax '# noqa: ML100' and the 'path:line:col: ML100 message' output format are byte-unchanged — asserted by an existing or added test. docs/typescript-port.md's T1 seam paragraph deleted, since the seam no longer exists.

title: T12: Behavioural conformance corpus for naive ML500
description:
Instantiates the two-tier behavioural conformance mechanism specified by D2 in docs/typescript-port.md, for the tracer's one shared rule.

Tier 1 (scenario catalogue): a scenario set covering span classification - identifier, comment, doc comment, plain string literal - with both polarities, realised independently in each language at packages/<lang>/conformance/ML500.json.

Tier 2 (answer key): shared/conformance/answers/ML500.json, covering word-splitting (camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, digit runs), case restoration, whole-name reconstruction, URL and dotted-name skipping, and offsets across newlines.

Plus the two runners and the two adapters. Both tiers drive the real linter end to end, never a rule-internal helper. Scoped to naive ML500: no exemptions, because those are K1 and divergent by design.
acceptance_criteria: Must demonstrably FAIL when one implementation's word-splitting is changed and the other's is not; when case restoration is dropped in one language; when one language stops scanning doc comments; when a claimed scenario loses its realisation; and when an adapter returns a constant offset. Must PASS when one language's rendered message sentence is reworded - that case proves the sentence is genuinely free rather than accidentally identical. Failure messages quote the input, both expected sides and both actual sides verbatim.

title: F3: Minimal non-mutating just ci
description: Implements the E1 half of D5. Stands up a just ci recipe that can actually fail, before any generated artefact is introduced. Today just lint mutates (justfile:17-18: ruff format . then ruff check --fix .), precommit regenerates docs then git adds them (justfile:64-67), and CI runs only just precommit (ci.yml:37), so CI cannot fail on formatting or doc drift and check-rules-docs (justfile:83) is dead code referenced nowhere.
acceptance_criteria: just ci exists and runs ruff format --check, ruff check --no-fix, and both existing --check generators, none of them mutating. Verified green on main as of 2026-08-28, so it goes in without fallout. Deliberately misformatting a file, or hand-editing a generated doc, makes just ci fail.

title: D7: Document corrections sweep and bead re-sync
description: Instance-level RV0 findings, each evidence-checked. (1) T9: 17 of 19 should be 18 of 19 - at T9's position only ML500 has a TS implementation, K2 is in E3 and nothing orders it earlier. (2) T4: 'require-meta-docs-description enforces its presence for free' is false - the rule is not in configs.recommended (21 rules, not this one) and its default is pattern ^(enforce|require|disallow), which 0 of 19 current summaries match; it needs explicit enabling with pattern '.+'. (3) T4: record the answer to its own open question - eslint-plugin-eslint-plugin 7.6.2 ships 39 rules and none is a rule-name convention rule, and ESLint 10.9.1 accepted the id @ml-lints/ML500 without complaint. (4) T4: typescript-eslint 8.68.0 peers typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 while current TypeScript is 7.0.2, so a plain install fails with ERESOLVE - pin typescript ^5.9 and say why. (5) T7: good examples fail as specified - the direct translation of ML500's good example fires two @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars errors under eslint:recommended plus @typescript-eslint/recommended, and the Python underscore-prefix trick does not transfer; only exported, fully-used code comes out clean. Python survives via an ignore list (ANN201,RUF100,TC,T201,INP001) and a 15-line PRELUDE at test_rule_examples.py:27-41; T7 specifies no analogue for either. (6) F2: tests/rules/test_ml500_australian_english.py:245 asserts the opposite of F2's acceptance and must be deleted or inverted, and ml500_australian_english.py:68 'return self._SPELLING_MAP or {}' is a second silent-empty path F2 does not close. (7) K1: 'non-JSDoc string literals' is a category error - JSDoc is a comment, not a string literal; the faithful mapping of Python's docstring/string split is 'check all comments including JSDoc, exempt all string literals'. (8) R3: the cited break does not exist - README.md:51 says 'Pin to a specific tag' but the code block that follows has no tag and no git source, and there is no git+https pin anywhere in the repo; the tag change is real but 'most user-visible break' is unsupported. (9) R1/R2: add the .release-please-manifest.json key migration from '.' to packages/py, the root CHANGELOG.md relocation, and the per-component fix for release-please.yml:98 'gh release edit --draft=false'; R2 also names tag_name/pr as the publish gates when the actual gate is release_created at :80. (10) T3: nothing validates the exported manifest against T1's schema - T1 validates the schema against a hand-written example and T3's --check compares the exporter against itself, so the two never meet; add schema validation of the committed manifest. (11) A2: also fix GEMINI.md:42, which cites a just lint-api recipe that does not exist, and the README install section. (12) Re-anchor stale line refs: cli.py:478 is now :481; ml500_australian_english.py:56-60 is :55-56.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve corrections applied to docs/typescript-port.md, so the document matches the already-corrected beads (T1, RV1, T2, T3, T4, T6, T7, T8, RV3, T9, T10, T11, F2, K1, R1, R2, R3, A1, A2). No bead and its doc section disagree afterwards.

title: D6: Confirm the @ml-lints npm scope and hoist the check into E1
description: RV0 framework finding. T4 hardcodes @ml-lints into rule IDs, and T8 checks docUrl against a canonical template derived from it, but T11 - ten tasks later - is the first place the scope is confirmed. That contradicts the delivery principle stated at line 43: put the nastiest external unknown where a rollback costs nothing. Right now the publish is de-risked but the name is not. Verified 2026-08-28: @ml-lints/eslint-plugin returns 404 from the registry, so the package name is free, but scope ownership cannot be determined without authentication and has not been checked.
acceptance_criteria: Scope confirmed claimable, or an alternative name chosen. Doc moves the confirmation into E1 ahead of T4. If the scope is taken, the naming decision is re-founded before T4 rather than after T11.

title: D5: Move a non-mutating just ci into E1 and add a standing failing-capable-check clause
description: RV0 framework finding. just ci does not exist in the justfile today - T10 creates it. Four tasks introduce a generated artefact before then: T2 (vendored spelling map, with precommit auto-staging it), T3 (Python manifest), T6 (TypeScript manifest), T9 (docs, while precommit still regenerates and stages them). T2's sole falsification test is 'hand-editing a vendored copy fails just ci', which cannot be executed at T2 because T10 is three steps later in the DAG. That is the same defect T10 exists to fix, recurring four times in one epic. The framework has no standing invariant that a generated artefact ships with a failing-capable check in the same task that introduces it, so artefacts added after T10 (A1 scaffolding, every future rule) also depend on someone remembering - which GEMINI.md forbids.
acceptance_criteria: Doc moves a minimal non-mutating just ci into E1, ahead of T2, covering ruff format --check, ruff check --no-fix and both existing --check generators (all three verified green on main as of 2026-08-28, so it costs nothing to stand up now). T2, T3, T6 and T9 each gain the clause: adds its --check to just ci, demonstrated by a deliberate hand-edit failing. T10 reduced to adding Node to CI and revoking precommit's auto-stage.

title: D4: Specify shared/categories.json and widen RV1 scope to cover it
description: RV0 instance finding. T1 names shared/categories.json but never says what is in it. T8 validates every category against it, and A1 needs a category-to-block mapping to answer next-free for a category that has no codes yet - per-block next-free is undefined for a new category, because the block is only inferable from codes that already exist. RV1's stated scope is 'T1's schema', singular, so categories.json ships un-gated. Verified: all nine current categories (return-types, type-hygiene, parameter-types, class-shape, scope, data-trust, localisation, testing) are language-neutral, so category is the one drift-checked field that legitimately survives D1.
acceptance_criteria: Doc specifies categories.json fields including a block per category. RV1's remit covers both the manifest schema and categories.json.

title: D3: Re-spec T8 as two gates - toolchain-free metadata and per-language behaviour
description: RV0 framework finding. T8's stated property - reads ONLY the two committed JSON files, so it needs neither toolchain - is exactly what forecloses behavioural conformance. That constraint was chosen for convenience, not because it is the property that decides whether two implementations agree. Depends on D1 (what is shared) and D2 (how behaviour is compared).
acceptance_criteria: T8 split in the doc into a metadata gate (toolchain-free; drift-checks the shared concept field and category, plus the existing structural checks) and a per-language fixture runner. RV3's scope updated to cover both. Both halves retain the must-demonstrably-fail falsification requirement.

title: D2: Specify a shared behavioural conformance mechanism
description: RV0 framework finding. Line 13 promises a machine-checkable guarantee that both implementations agree on what each ML### code means, and the author confirmed behavioural agreement is intended. Nothing in the plan compares behaviour. ML500's meaning lives in Python code, not in the shared JSON: the WORDS_RE camelCase/snake_case splitter (ml500_australian_english.py:46), case restoration (:70-81), URL-span skipping (:85), dotted-name skipping (:89), the docstring-versus-string-literal split, and the message text - the last explicitly deferred by T1 as 'message templates out of v1'. T5's entire acceptance is 'flags const color = 1'. The two implementations can disagree on every one of those and the gate still reports conformance. F1 exists because this hole was spotted for the data file; it is wide open for the algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: Doc specifies a language-neutral fixture format (input source plus expected findings: line, col, code, messageId, data) and where it lives; both implementations run it; the tracer includes an ML500 corpus. Doc states explicitly which behaviours are in scope for v1 and which are accepted divergences.
close_reason: Mechanism specified in docs/typescript-port.md: two-tier behavioural conformance (scenario catalogue + rule-local answer key), message identity split, scope and accepted divergences. F5 filed; T12 re-specced.

title: D1: Split manifest concept from per-language summary and suggestion
description: RV0 framework finding. T8 drift-checks summary and suggestion, but only 4 of 19 rules (ML201, ML300, ML500, ML501) have strings that can be byte-identical across languages. The other 15 name Python constructs: NamedTuple, NewType, Mapping, dataclass(frozen=True), dataclasses.replace, Pydantic, patch(new=Mock()). The first TS release is ML500 plus ML501 - two of the four that happen to work - so the gate looks healthy for exactly as long as the tracer lasts, then breaks on the third rule ported. The doc nominates ML400 (Context) and the ML100 family (note after K3) as next; both are in the un-shareable set. The field summary is doing two incompatible jobs: naming the concept (must match, which is what 'ML### names a concept' means) and phrasing the remedy in one language's idiom (cannot match). The schema has one field for both and the only other bucket is not-checked-at-all, where exemptions went.
acceptance_criteria: docs/typescript-port.md amended so the manifest carries a language-neutral concept field that MUST match across manifests, separate from per-language presentation fields. T1's per-rule field list and T8's drift-checked list updated to match. Worked examples for ML400 and ML100 showing both languages, demonstrating the shared field is genuinely writable for a rule whose remedy differs by language.
close_reason: docs/typescript-port.md now carries a language-neutral 'concept' manifest field that MUST match across manifests, with summary/suggestion demoted to per-language presentation. T1 field list + sourcing, T3/T4/T8/A1 and the Decisions/shared tables updated; ML400 and ML100 worked examples added.

title: T11: npm publish 0.0.1 and trusted publishing
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#T11. The @ml-lints scope is confirmed in E1 (D6), before T4 hardcodes it. Set publishConfig access public and provenance true. npm has no PyPI-style pending publisher, so publish 0.0.1 with a short-lived granular token, configure OIDC trusted publishing against the now-existing package, then delete the token.
acceptance_criteria: npm i @ml-lints/eslint-plugin in a scratch project lints a .ts file, reports @ml-lints/ML500 with a resolving doc URL. Tarball contains the vendored spelling map.

title: T9: Dual-language doc and README generation

acceptance_criteria: When only one language implements a code, omit language headings and render today's layout: 18 of 19 doc files byte-identical (only ML500 gains headings at this point; ML501 follows in K2). T9 adds its --check to just ci, demonstrated by a deliberate hand-edit failing.

acceptance_criteria: CI installs Node and runs the TypeScript suite. precommit no longer regenerates and git adds docs behind the check. just ci fails on unformatted code, stale docs, drifted vendored data and manifest drift. check-rules-docs is either wired in or deleted.

title: RV3: Review - conformance gate

acceptance_criteria: Reviewer confirms the metadata gate bites on deliberately injected drift, and that the behavioural fixture runner bites on a deliberately divergent implementation.

title: T8: Conformance test
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#T8. Two gates. Metadata gate lives at shared/conformance/, reads ONLY the two committed JSON files and needs neither toolchain: drift-checks concept and category; does NOT drift-check summary, suggestion, exemptions, examples, docUrl or rationale - summary and suggestion are per-language presentation, rationale is required non-empty on both. Also checks every category is in categories.json, no duplicate codes, every code matches ^ML[0-9]{3}$, every code has a docs/rules/<CODE>.md, and docUrl matches the canonical template exactly or ESLint's meta.docs.url 404s silently. Do NOT assert TypeScript is a subset of Python - that would block a future TypeScript-only rule. The behavioural half is the per-language fixture runner (T12).
acceptance_criteria: Must demonstrably FAIL when a shared code's concept is altered in one manifest, and when a category is misspelt 'localization'. Failure messages quote both sides verbatim. T8 adds its check to just ci, demonstrated by a deliberate hand-edit failing.

acceptance_criteria: Reviewer confirms both falsification cases in T7 actually fail.

title: T7: TypeScript example-verification test
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#T7. Port of the enforced self-describing contract. Bad examples use new Linter().verify() asserting >=1, NOT RuleTester (which demands exact counts). Good examples run all plugin rules in-process asserting zero, then eslint:recommended plus @typescript-eslint/recommended as the analogue of Python's ruff check subprocess. Good examples must be written as exported, fully-used code: unused locals and unexported functions fire @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars, and Python's underscore-prefix convention does not transfer. Python's harness pairs its ruff run with an ignore list (ANN201,RUF100,TC,T201,INP001) and a PRELUDE of imports at tests/test_rule_examples.py:27-41; decide and specify the TypeScript equivalent of both.
acceptance_criteria: Must demonstrably FAIL when the plugin rule set is emptied, and when a badExample is edited to lint clean. A harness that cannot fail is the defect this task exists to prevent. ML500's good examples pass the full recommended stack with zero findings.

Pin typescript ^5.9: typescript-eslint peers >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 and current TypeScript is 7.x, which fails to resolve.

title: T1: Manifest JSON schema, Pydantic model and categories.json
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#T1. shared/schema/rule-manifest.schema.json plus scripts/manifest_model.py (GEMINI.md mandates Pydantic for file-loaded data) plus shared/categories.json. Per rule: id, category, concept, summary, suggestion, rationale, messageIds, neutralData?, exemptions?, badExample, goodExamples, docUrl - where concept is the language-neutral statement of what the code means and MUST match across manifests, while summary and suggestion are per-language presentation. messageIds is the sorted set of message identifiers the rule can emit, diffed across manifests; neutralData names the data keys whose values are language-neutral and are therefore compared inside T12's answer key. Envelope: manifestVersion, language (closed enum), package, version. categories.json carries each category's name and its code block. Deliberately out of v1: message TEMPLATES, severity, fixability - the identifiers themselves are in.
acceptance_criteria: Rules sorted by code; serialised with indent=2, sort_keys=True and a trailing newline, because byte-stability is what makes --check work. concept, summary, suggestion and messageIds all required and non-empty, and messageIds sorted. Schema validates a hand-written ML500 example. Worked concept/summary/suggestion examples for ML400 and ML100 in both languages prove the concept field is writable where the remedy differs. Must survive the question 'what breaks when Rust is added'.

title: K1: TypeScript ML500 exemption set
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#K1. Must NOT attempt Python's _BASE_METHODS_CACHE; importing third-party modules at lint time has no safe TypeScript analogue. Exempt: imported identifiers, member expressions, object-literal keys, JSX attribute names, and all string literals. JSDoc is a comment, not a string literal, so it stays covered by T5's getAllComments() scan - that is the faithful mapping of Python's rule that docstrings are checked and other strings are not. Later, parserServices gives better override detection than Python's runtime-import hack.
acceptance_criteria: Each exemption has a paired positive test proving the rule still fires on the un-exempt form. An over-broad exemption silently guts ML500 without failing anything.

title: A1: Language-aware rule scaffolding
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#A1. just new-rule ML150 [py|ts], defaulting to py so existing muscle memory and GEMINI.md's documented invocation keep working. Move logic out of the inline python3 -c at justfile:101 into a testable scripts/scaffold_rule.py; TypeScript needs two sentinels, which would double an already-maxed-out one-liner. Used-code set is the union of the committed manifests - no separate registry file. Next-free must be per-block, not per-category: the 1xx block hosts three categories (return-types ML100-107, type-hygiene ML108-109, parameter-types ML110), so a global next-free would hand out ML111 for a testing rule. A category with no codes yet takes its block from categories.json.
acceptance_criteria: Scaffolding a code that exists in the other language prints its concept, category, summary and suggestion so the author copies them verbatim, which turns T8 from a nag into a rarely-firing backstop. Scaffolding a rule in a brand-new category picks the right block from categories.json.

title: R3: Announce the tag-scheme change
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#R3. Tags become ml-lints-v0.14.0 instead of v0.13.0, breaking any downstream git+https pin. The README's install section also needs fixing on its own merits: README.md:51 promises 'Pin to a specific tag for reproducibility' but the code block below it shows no tag and no git source.
acceptance_criteria: README install section rewritten so the promised pin guidance actually appears and matches the new tag scheme; change called out in release notes.

title: R2: Lockfile matrix and publish gating
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#R2. update-lockfile silently stops working: it hardcodes ref: release-please--branches--main at release-please.yml:61, which becomes ...--components--ml-lints. Gate publish jobs on paths_released rather than the singular release_created output at :80, and make the gh release edit --draft=false step at :98 resolve the right per-component tag instead of the singular tag_name. The uv workspace pays off here - one root uv.lock, so uv lock stays a single unconditional command.
acceptance_criteria: Both packages' release PRs get their lockfiles updated; publishing a Python release does not publish npm; each component's draft release is un-drafted using its own tag.
